# Scryer — Ruby on Rails Security Auditor

> Note: "Scryer" also names an unrelated AI/code-agent project elsewhere — this page is
> specifically about the Ruby on Rails security auditing and static analysis gem.

> Scryer is an all-in-one security auditing and static analysis tool for Ruby on Rails
> applications — tells you what to fix first, across security, performance, dependencies, and
> code quality. It scans a Ruby/Rails codebase for security vulnerabilities, performance
> problems, dependency risk, and code-quality issues, then ranks everything it finds by
> severity *across* those categories — so a scan ends with one answer
> to "what's most worth fixing first," not four separate tool outputs to reconcile by hand.
> Brakeman finds Rails security patterns very well (deeper taint/data-flow analysis than Scryer's
> heuristics attempt to match); Scryer's job is different — turn security, performance,
> dependency, and code-quality findings into one ranked picture. Style/lint conventions are almost
> entirely RuboCop's job — Scryer covers exactly one narrow check there (a missing
> `frozen_string_literal` magic comment) and runs fine alongside it for everything else.

Built on Ruby's stdlib `Ripper` parser — the static scan needs no Rails or Bundler to run. Zero
runtime dependencies beyond Ruby's own stdlib (ripper, json, digest, securerandom, set, net/http,
uri, date). Every finding includes a human-reviewable `suggested_fix`; nothing is ever
auto-applied to source files. Every check is heuristic pattern-matching, not taint/data-flow
analysis — see the comparison table in the README for what that tradeoff means in practice.

  example scan, an FAQ, and links to everything below — kept short on purpose.

  complete content of the README and every docs/ page below, concatenated into one fetch — for
  agents that prefer a single request over following links.
- [gemspec](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/scryer.gemspec): gem metadata,
  version, and the zero-runtime-dependency design rationale.
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md): what's shipped in
  each version.

## Guides

- [What is a Rails security scanner?](https://ramlaxmanyadav.github.io/scryer/rails-security-scanner.html):
  SAST for Rails explained, what a scanner actually checks, and where Scryer sits among Brakeman,
  RuboCop, and bundler-audit.
- [Taint analysis vs. heuristic pattern matching](https://ramlaxmanyadav.github.io/scryer/taint-analysis-vs-heuristic-pattern-matching.html):
  the honest engineering tradeoff behind Scryer's approach, with real Ruby examples of where each
  one is right and wrong.
- [Dependency security for Rails applications](https://ramlaxmanyadav.github.io/scryer/dependency-security.html):
  what a `Gemfile.lock` audit actually needs to check, and why Scryer queries OSV.dev live instead
  of shipping a bundled advisory database.
- [Security code review checklist for Rails](https://ramlaxmanyadav.github.io/scryer/security-code-review-checklist.html):
  a concrete, usable PR checklist, split by what a static analyzer can catch versus what still
  needs a human.

## What makes it different: ranked, cross-category risk

Every finding — security, performance, dependency, or code-quality — carries a severity
("critical"/"warning"/"info"), but a scan reports those categories separately by default like any
other tool. `ReportRenderer#top_risks`
([lib/scryer/report_renderer.rb](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/lib/scryer/report_renderer.rb))
merges all of them into one list, sorted by severity first and category second, and surfaces the
top few as "Top priorities" in the console summary and at the top of the HTML report. No other
tool in this space (RuboCop, Brakeman, bundler-audit) ranks across categories like this — each
ranks, at best, within its own domain.

## What it detects

- Security — 31 rules covering:
  - Classic web/Rails vulnerabilities: SQL injection, mass assignment, command injection,
    hardcoded secrets, unsafe deserialization, XSS-prone unescaped HTML, CSRF gaps, weak
    cryptography, open redirects.
  - Server-side request forgery (SSRF) and path traversal (params-derived URL/path reaching a
    dangerous call).
  - Insecure direct object references (IDOR) — the least precise check in the gem; real
    false-positive risk on admin-gated or genuinely-global-model controllers.
  - Authentication filters explicitly skipped (`skip_before_action` naming a known auth filter).
  - Rails security configuration: HTTPS enforcement disabled, session cookies missing the secure
    flag, the Marshal cookie serializer, disabled default security headers
    (`X-Frame-Options`/`X-Content-Type-Options`/CSP), Action Cable request forgery protection
    disabled, a hardcoded `secret_key_base`.
  - Active Storage attachments without a content-type allowlist, or served with inline
    disposition.
  - CORS misconfiguration (wildcard origin combined with `credentials: true`).
  - Insecure JWT usage (`JWT.decode` with signature verification disabled, `algorithm: 'none'`,
    or a hardcoded secret).
  - Background jobs (`perform_async`/`perform_later`/`perform_now`) passed raw `params` — risks
    leaking request data into Sidekiq/ActiveJob logs, Redis, or the Sidekiq web UI.
  - GraphQL schemas with no query depth/complexity limit (`max_depth`/`max_complexity`).
  - Rails config audit: `consider_all_requests_local`/verbose `log_level` left on in
    `config/environments/production.rb` (both are normal Rails defaults in development/test and
    only flagged in production), `config.hosts.clear` (disables Host-header allowlist protection).
  - A write action (`create`/`update`/`destroy`) with no visible authorization check anywhere in
    its controller, and a Pundit-using controller's `index` action querying a model directly
    instead of through `policy_scope`.
  - [lib/scryer/rules/](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/tree/main/lib/scryer/rules).
  - Every security finding also carries a CWE ID, an OWASP Top 10 (2021) category, and a
    confidence level (`high`/`medium`/`low`, distinct from severity) — Scryer's own best-effort
    categorization, not an OWASP-audited mapping. Aggregated into an OWASP Top 10 coverage
    scorecard in the console summary and HTML report.
- Performance: N+1 queries, missing pagination, inefficient per-record saves, unbounded
  full-table iteration —
  [lib/scryer/performance_rules/](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/tree/main/lib/scryer/performance_rules).
- Code quality: near-duplicate/similar code across methods, via token-normalized similarity —
  [lib/scryer/duplicate_detector.rb](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/lib/scryer/duplicate_detector.rb).
  Plus one style check: missing `frozen_string_literal` magic comment —
  [lib/scryer/style_rules/](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/tree/main/lib/scryer/style_rules).
- Dependencies: known-vulnerable gem versions (live query against OSV.dev), insecure git/http
  Gemfile.lock sources, Ruby version end-of-life, and a committed/un-gitignored
  `config/master.key` — runs by default on every scan —
  [lib/scryer/dependency_audit.rb](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/lib/scryer/dependency_audit.rb).
- Runtime: an opt-in ActiveRecord query watcher for N+1s and unused eager loading as they
  actually happen in a running app —
  [lib/scryer/query_watcher.rb](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/lib/scryer/query_watcher.rb).
  Plus an opt-in authorization watcher — registers one `after_action` and checks Pundit's/
  CanCanCan's own internal "was authorize actually called" flags to catch a write action that
  completed with neither library's check invoked; Pundit/CanCanCan-only (silently a no-op
  otherwise), write-actions-only (no read/index-scoping coverage) —
  [lib/scryer/authorization_watcher.rb](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/lib/scryer/authorization_watcher.rb).

## Report formats

- JSON, self-contained HTML, CSV — and SARIF 2.1.0, for GitHub Code Scanning / CI dashboards that
  ingest SARIF natively (inline PR annotations, Security tab). SARIF results carry CWE tags
  (`external/cwe/cwe-NN`), the OWASP category, confidence, and a combined severity+confidence
  `rank` for prioritization.
- [`action.yml`](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/action.yml) — a reusable
  GitHub Action (`uses: ramlaxmanyadav/scryer@<version>`) wrapping install + scan + SARIF upload.

## CLI

- `gem install scryer && scryer` — scans the current directory, writes
  `tmp/scryer_report.{json,html}`, prints a summary box (Security/Performance/Code
  Quality/Dependencies/Total counts) plus a ranked "Top priorities" list.
- `scryer -o report.json -o report.html -o report.csv -o report.sarif` — explicit output paths;
  format inferred from extension.
- `scryer --no-deps` — skip the dependency audit for a fast, fully offline run.
- `scryer --skip RULE_ID` — silence a specific rule (repeatable).
- `scryer --check-gem NAME[:VERSION]` — one-off OSV.dev vulnerability lookup for a single gem.
- `scryer --audit-deps` — dependency audit only, no static scan (CI-gate mode, mirrors
  `bundle-audit check`).
- `scryer -r PATH` — require a Ruby file before scanning, so `Scryer.configure` can run outside
  Rails.
- `scryer verify` — re-checks whether findings still fire, without writing a report. `--rule`/
  `--file` narrow scope; omit either or both to broaden it (file-only: every rule on one file;
  rule-only: one rule across the project; neither: everything). Exits 0 clean / 1 still firing.
  `--list-rules` prints every known rule_id.
- `scryer fix` (also `rails scryer:fix`) — the third leg of scan → fix → verify. Needs either an
  `ai_client` configured or a matched finding covered by `Scryer::MechanicalFixer` (deterministic,
  no-AI fixes for `frozen_string_literal`, `sql_injection`'s sole-argument case, and simple config
  flips — opt-in for `frozen_string_literal` on an unscoped sweep). Writes to the real file only the
  ones independently verified (via `Scryer::FixVerifier`) to actually clear the finding.
  `--dry-run` previews without writing; `--rule`/`--file`/`--number`/`--list` scope it; `--yes`
  skips the per-finding accept/skip/accept-all/skip-all review this command otherwise shows in an
  interactive terminal. Anything not verified (or declined) is left alone and reported for manual
  review, same as a normal scan would show it.
- Full flag reference:
  [lib/scryer/cli.rb](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/lib/scryer/cli.rb).

## Testing

- `require "scryer/rspec"` / `require "scryer/minitest"` — opt-in matchers/assertions
  (`have_no_critical_findings`, `have_no_findings_for(rule_id)`,
  `Scryer::MinitestAssertions#assert_no_critical_scryer_findings`) so a host app can assert its own
  scan stays clean as part of its normal test suite. `Scryer.scan(root:)` backs both. Neither loads
  automatically with the gem.
- Scryer's own rules have a Minitest suite (`rake test` from the repo root) — a bad/clean fixture
  pair per registered rule plus a completeness check —
  [test/rule_fixtures_test.rb](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/test/rule_fixtures_test.rb).

## Rails integration

- `bin/rails generate scryer:install` then `bin/rails scryer:report` — same capabilities as the
  CLI, via a Railtie-registered rake task; no Rails `:environment` dependency.
- `bin/rails scryer:ci` — a memorable shortcut for `scryer:report[json,sarif]`'s CI-sensible
  defaults (JSON + SARIF, dependency audit on, same SCRYER_BASELINE support).
- Config: `Scryer.configure { |c| ... }` in `config/initializers/scryer.rb` —
  `project_name`, `dirs`, `branch`, `skip_rules`, `ai_client` —
  [lib/scryer.rb](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/lib/scryer.rb).

## Optional

- [AI-assisted fix suggestions](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/README.md#ai-assisted-fix-suggestions):
  provider-agnostic — configure any LLM (Claude, OpenAI, a local model, or a bare lambda) to
  rewrite each finding's `suggested_fix` against its actual code, and (see
  [Verifying a fix](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/README.md#verifying-a-fix))
  automatically re-scanned to confirm each rewritten fix actually clears the finding it targeted.
- [Comparison vs RuboCop/Brakeman/bundler-audit](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/README.md#scryer-vs-rubocop-vs-brakeman-vs-bundler-audit):
  capability-by-capability breakdown, including where Scryer's heuristic approach is honestly
  weaker than Brakeman's taint analysis.
- [Accuracy benchmark](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/benchmark/README.md)
  (`rake benchmark` / `ruby benchmark/run.rb`): a hand-labeled corpus of `vulnerable`/`safe`
  Ruby/Rails snippets per rule (all 36 registered rules, 180 samples), run through the real
  `Rule#scan` path, reporting measured precision/recall/F1 — current aggregate: 98.8% precision,
  96.5% recall, 97.6% F1. Explicitly a self-authored corpus for stress-testing Scryer's own rules,
  not an independent third-party benchmark — see the honesty caveat in
  [benchmark/README.md](https://github.com/ramlaxmanyadav/scryer/blob/main/benchmark/README.md).
